page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations position the D8s_v4 in the average performance tier for most standard operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1411.98 and 7435.42 respectively, both falling within the middle 50% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is measured at 414.43 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, and 44.87 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves 23.82 GB/sec, while bzip3 decompression shows weaker performance, scoring 8.78 GB/sec on single-threaded and 25.34 GB/sec on multi-threaded tasks. Geekbench testing reports a single-core score of 1155.0 and a multi-core score of 4610.0.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, the D8s_v4 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring stable, dedicated compute resources without the overhead of local NVMe drives. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving (demonstrating 6.85 GB/sec throughput), database operations (Passmark database score of 2861.21), and Redis caching (6.84 million SET operations per second). It is less optimal for heavy single-threaded decompression or large-scale LLM inference, where its prompt processing speeds for small models are relatively weak.
